messages:
Maya Patel: Quick idea: run a compact "mini-lab" launch — 20-min live walkthrough + 20-min Q&A. Bundle: tiny tutorial (vector search + streaming), reproducible benchmark notebook, and a 2-file refapp. Objective: dev signups + GitHub stars.
Liam O'Connor: Sounds good. What's the target audience? devs trying to add cheap embeddings + streaming chat?
Maya Patel: Exactly. Audience = product/ML engineers exploring inference cost vs latency. Emphasize 'replayable' benchmarks they can run locally.
Rosa Kim: I'll draft the tutorial. Plan to keep it 700-900 words, steps: 1) clone refapp, 2) set REDWOOD_API_KEY, 3) run `make demo`, 4) inspect results/bench.ipynb.
Evan Brooks: For the benchmark, recommend a small Jupyter that hits both Hosted and Dedicated endpoints and compares p50/p95 + tokens/second. Example curl test to include in notebook:
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"community-search@v1", "input":"summarize: " + readme, "max_tokens":128}'
```
I'll add a helper that runs 30 requests and prints med/95/throughput.
Taylor Nguyen: Landing page needs clear CTA. Propose: "RSVP for the mini-lab" (collect email + role + company_size). Post-event CTA: 'Clone the refapp' + 'Start free hosted trial' link.
Maya Patel: Add hidden field `priority` with (evaluation, pilot, procurement) so sales can triage. Also add `region` (NA/EU/APAC).
Liam O'Connor: Lead routing: Ops Bot will send each RSVP to #marketing-leads and create a HubSpot contact. Mapping: email->email, company_size->company_size, utm_source->campaign. Add `priority` tag.
Ops Bot: webhook test: /integrations/hubspot/mini-lab posted -> ok.
Rosa Kim: Repo name? I'd prefer `community-mini-lab-vector-search` to differentiate from previous refapps.
Evan Brooks: Agreed. I'll seed the repo with bench.ipynb + demo server. We'll keep it private until launch day (open on publish).
Taylor Nguyen: Promo timeline: announce blog post Apr 2, tutorial publish Apr 6, tutorial video (90s) Apr 8, webinar Apr 12. Sequence: blog -> social -> email invite -> reminder 48h + 2h before.
Maya Patel: We should test the live run. Backup plan: pre-recorded bench run and a lightweight model fallback `community-search-small` in case the main pool is noisy.
Liam O'Connor: Ops note: ensure API quota for the live demo. I'll reserve a small Dedicated slot for the run window (Apr 12 10:00-11:00 UTC).
Rosa Kim: Tutorial snippet for config to paste:
```
# config.yaml
api_key: $REDWOOD_API_KEY
endpoint: https://api.redwood.ai/v1
model: community-search@v1
```
Keep example values minimal.
Evan Brooks: Example Python helper to run bench (to include in notebook):
```
import requests, time
for i in range(30):
  start=time.time()
  r=requests.post(url,json=payload,headers=headers)
  print(i, r.status_code, len(r.text), time.time()-start)
```
We'll convert to async later.
Taylor Nguyen: Messaging: lead with "replayable benchmarks" and a subhead "run the same tests we do in <10m". Short social: "See p50/p95, tokens/sec, and cost — live. RSVP."
Maya Patel: I'll draft three subject lines for the invite: 1) "Mini-lab: Repro Bench + Vector Refapp" 2) "See inference cost & latency live" 3) "Build a streaming vector search in 10 minutes".
Liam O'Connor: Who's presenting? Maya + Evan for demo, Rosa for tutorial walkthrough. Taylor to moderate Q&A.
Ops Bot: Reminder scheduled: dry-run on Apr 10 16:00 UTC -> invites sent.
Rosa Kim: Asset asks: hero image (dev at terminal), 30s screencap for social, and a GIF of demo. Can design deliver by Apr 6? @design?
Taylor Nguyen: Yes, I'll ping design and request 2 variants for A/B testing.
Evan Brooks: Small ask: include a short README in repo with a `results/` folder containing a sample `benchmark_summary.json` so people without infra can still see numbers.
Maya Patel: Great. Also, include a small section in the tutorial on how to interpret p50 vs p95 and why batching matters. Make it friendly for non-experts.
Liam O'Connor: GDPR note: add explicit consent checkbox on form + link to privacy policy.
Taylor Nguyen: I'll include `utm_campaign=mini-lab-vecsearch` and tag the email flow.
Rosa Kim: Review windows: tutorial draft by Apr 4, repo seed by Apr 5, landing copy by Apr 6. Who's OK to review? Maya/Evan for tech; Taylor for copy.
Maya Patel: I'll review Apr 4 afternoon.
Evan Brooks: I'll review repo Apr 5 morning.
Taylor Nguyen: I'll review landing Apr 6 morning.
Ops Bot: all tasks posted to marketing board card: "mini-lab: replayable benchmark & vector refapp".
Maya Patel: Ok team — final check: CTA = RSVP, post-event CTA = repo + free hosted trial. Keep messaging practical and numbers-first. Thumbs if we proceed. :white_check_mark: 
Maya Patel: :thumbsup:
Liam O'Connor: :thumbsup:
Rosa Kim: :thumbsup:
Evan Brooks: :thumbsup:
Taylor Nguyen: :thumbsup:
Ops Bot: thread note: archived after launch.
